notes.title: Coming to Nintendo Switch 2 this Winter! Check out the first demo at Gamescom!
notes.notes:
Thanks to everyone's feedback and support, development has been progressing very smoothly and we are super excited to announce that [b]we're bringing [i]Glaciered[/i] to the Nintendo Switch 2![/b]

We were also incredibly fortunate to have had the opportunity to be featured on Nintendo's official online Indie showcase, [i]Indie World 2025.8.7[/i].

Please check out Glaciered's segment here↓. 
[previewyoutube=Iy3wbs9tdtM;full][/previewyoutube]
But wait there's more, from August 20 to August 24, at [i]gamescom 2025[/i], one of the world's largest gaming events held at Koelnmesse in Cologne, Germany, we will be showcasing the very first playable demo of the Nintendo Switch 2 version at the Nintendo corner of the Indie Arena Booth (Kiosk No. N4). 
We will also have an exclusive novelty item prepared, so please be sure to stop by our booth and play the demo if you are attending!

Gamescom Official Site：[url=https://www.gamescom.global/en]https://www.gamescom.global/en[/url]

The Nintendo Switch 2 version is scheduled for release this Winter, but we will continue to reveal new information on the game in the days leading up to its release, so stay tuned!

notes.title: Demo Updated for Steam Next Fest!
notes.notes:
Hello, I'm Shibuya from Studio Snowblind, the developer of Glaciered.

The Steam demo has been updated for Steam Next Fest, which will start on June 9. This update focuses on improving core gameplay and QOL features, and this was achieved by building upon the feedback we've received from the community.

[url=https://discord.gg/g6yn9gYU69][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/ec97cb5f1ab0f398bcf64d8fa44a8ce058488321.gif[/img][/url]
Please join our official Discord channel to directly send me your thoughts!

[h2]English Voiceover Added[/h2]
We've added an English voiceover to the game! I'm very happy to be able to make the game more immersive for non-Japanese speakers.

The text language and voiceover language can be changed separately, so you could try out a different voiceover language for a new playthrough for a fresh experience!

[h2]New Feature: Knowledge[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/7ef22682a59780c6d9e70a42ef438db1d301e952.jpg[/img]
We've added Knowledge, a new feature that digs deeper into the world of the game. Knowledge adds an encyclopedia on the creatures of the underwater world of Glaciered, including the ecology of various creatures and the culture of the Tuai, the player character’s species. You can unlock Knowledge by progressing through the story and completing quests.

Unlocking Knowledge about a creature grants you a bonus that increases the amount of experience you gain from defeating said creature. And with the addition of this feature, names and levels of creatures will no longer be displayed the first time you encounter them. This information will only be displayed once you’ve unlocked one or more Knowledge levels for that creature. We believe this will make for a more immersive experience.

Note: Save data created from the old demo version may not be able to unlock Knowledge. If this happens, please start a new save to experience the new feature.

[h2]Player Action Improvements[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/17cd7798319ec6cda8db4f43d560d30555a009ec.gif[/img]
The protagonist Gray can now fly at high speeds (i.e. in Strom Mode) in four directions: forwards, backwards, left, and right. This was a highly requested feature from the community. This change greatly improves maneuverability and freedom of movement.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/b1f55c44df000198e54212ad7175d82bd7bae78e.gif[/img]
We reworked all of Gray’s actions and adjusted the timing for canceling out of attacks, input buffering, and input delay. This makes the action more responsive and satisfying to play.

We’ve also reworked the timing for perfect dodges. Before, there was a slight delay between the dodge input and the perfect dodge judgment. Now, the judgment is made on the very first frame of the dodge. This should make perfect dodges more intuitive.

[h2]Camera Improvements[/h2]
Before, the camera was restricted to not go behind terrain features, which made it prone to stuttering in tight spaces or when right next to a wall. This has been alleviated by making walls and ceilings turn transparent when they get between the camera and Gray. This should improve camera stability and make it easier to fight in tight spaces.

Moreover, I completely redesigned the aim down sights camera from scratch. This alleviated the issues of the camera getting stuck on objects and the inconsistent camera speeds while trying to aim. This makes aiming much smoother than before.

[h2]Creature Animation Improvements[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/975cada507097573e230f338f2958b3795ccaaf6.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/6d30a7fff3fbeac7c639973217ce3915160af4b6.gif[/img]
All of the character animation in Glaciered is handmade, but the game also computes procedural animations in real time and blends them with the handmade animations, resulting in more natural movements. This system has also been redesigned from the ground up.

Many creatures can now move even more naturally and smoothly than before. This should give them a more lasting impression and make battles feel more immersive.

Moreover, hitting an enemy with an attack will cause the point of impact to vibrate slightly afterwards. This should add more oomph to attacks and make it easier to discern where your attacks hit.

[h2]Balancing Tweaks[/h2]
[list]
[*]Raised the base damage of the special Shard Quills attack “Homing Crystals” from 16 to 18.
[*]Lowered the recovery speed of ranged crystal shards.
[*]Lowered the recovery amount of the Pui support skill Shard Recovery.
[/list]
[h2]QOL[/h2]
[list]
[*]Added a circular stamina gauge displayed next to the player character, which makes it easier to check remaining stamina amount in the midst of battle. The transparency of the stamina gauge can be changed in the options.
[*]Added a visual indicator of shot accuracy to the crosshair of ranged attacks. Shot accuracy increases when aiming down sights and decreases when hip firing.
[*]Subtitles are now displayed at the bottom of the screen by default instead of at the top. You can still choose to display them at the top in the options.
[*]Added a dark background to subtitles. This can be toggled in the options.
[*]Added the ability to change which screen to display the option menu on. This improves the gameplay experience in multi-screen setups.
[*]Added crosshair transparency options.
[*]Added new visual and sound effects and improved existing ones.
[*]Improved overall performance by preloading game data, changing to asynchronous processing for various tasks, and implementing GPU computing.
[/list]
[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the command to save your Pui to remain on the screen.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused enemy AI to stop responding upon retrying an encounter.
[*]Fixed a bug where the special variant in the demo endgame quest “Rite of the Hunt” was sometimes not randomized as intended.
[/list]
[h2]Removed Features[/h2]
[list]
[*]The motion blur feature has been removed. This was a trade-off done in order to add new graphics features and slightly improve performance.
[/list]
[h2]PAX East 2025 Report[/h2]
Lastly, I’d like to report on our demo showcase at PAX East 2025, back in May 5-May 10 at the Boston Convention and Exhibition Center.

I was happy to see players interested in worldbuilding aspects such as the story and underwater exploration, and players even raised some interesting ideas such as “I want to customize the Pui” and “I want to see an eel-like creature”.

Some players struggled with exploring and battling underwater due to the added verticality and expressed the want for difficulty options. The demo is currently fixed to Normal difficulty, but more difficulty options such as Easy and Hard will be added to the full version of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/f8fd494aa9a14a49ab6e291ab94d17a5af467be5.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/a4023c0958b72df01b09a8438769a88563af2ac6.png[/img]

notes.title: PAX East, New Trailer, and a Q3 2025 Release!
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

This is Shibuya from Studio Snowblind.

Glaciered will be showcased at PAX East, a gaming convention to be held at the Boston Convention and Exhibition Center from May 8 to May 11, 2025!

At the booth of PLAYISM, the publisher, the latest demo will be available for everyone to try, and we'll also be giving out free Glaciered goodies! Please check [url=https://east.paxsite.com/]the official PAX East website[/url] for more details on the event.

I'm pleasantly surprised by the enthusiastic response we've received ever since the release of the Glaciered demo last winter.

Taking everyone's valuable feedback into account for the full version of the game is one of our top priorities, and we've also been hard at work improving the camera, controls, growth mechanics, and more. We're actually planning on updating the demo soon in order to better reflect some of these improvements. More details will be announced in a patch notes post once the demo has been updated.

It's been around 3 years since I first announced this project, but we're finally able to aim for a Q3 2025 (around July to September) release! We're doing our best to deliver a good game of satisfying quality. Please be patient as we make the game the best it can be.

Here's a new trailer of some more content we've been working on. The sea 65 million years in the future has many different faces. This time, we introduced the Sea of Crises, where very little light shines through. Many creatures live here, and they all have tricky attacks, such as by using venom or ink. Here, you'll be challenged to change up your strategies compared to other areas.

[previewyoutube=PkV7iSxe0ko;full][/previewyoutube]
I'll continue to post updates and teaser content on the official Discord server, so please come in to take a peek if you're interested!

notes.title: Demo Hotfix v0.7.261
notes.notes:
Hello, thank you so much for playing the demo and giving us your valuable feedback!
We just released v0.7.261 demo hotfix, including

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where unintended values were being applied to certain things like enemy health and sound effect playback speed, resulting in super-tanky enemies and noise-like sound effects. This was mainly happening in French, German, and other specific regions.
[*] Fixed an issue where default weapons (wings) were unintentionally duplicated when switching save slots.
[*] Fixed an issue that under certain conditions, the number of items dropped by death would be greater than the number of items you had.
[*] Fixed an issue that ascending/descending stops working in certain cases.
[/list]

[h2]Minor Changes & QoL improvements[/h2]
[list]
[*] Updated the game engine to the latest version
[*] Added motion blur intensity to the option screen. (set 0 to turn motion blur off)
[*] You can now assign Ctrl, Alt, and other modifier keys to actions using the key mapping feature.
[*] ESC, Start (gamepad) and other specific keys should now be ignored.
[*] Tweaked the timings for the fast traveling tutorial
[*] The function to switch the lock-on target by camera input when using mouse & keyboard input has been disabled by default.

[i]Dev Note: This feature was not useful for the majority of mouse & keyboard users.
If you prefer to keep this feature, turn on the function in the options menu.[/i]
[/list]

[h2]Balance Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Increased damage modifier to Guedu vulnerable spots to 1.4 from 1.2
[*] Increased base damage of Guedu charge attack to 60 from 50

[i]Dev Note: To avoid the fight with Guedu becoming too long, we have increased the benefit of attacking their vulnerable spots where the risk is high but more rewarding.
The Rush Bite, which is easy to avoid, has had its damage increased to keep them threatening.[/i]
[/list]

We have also updated the game engine to the latest version with this update. This has required repackaging existing data, making the size of the patch larger than usual. Thank you for your understanding.

We really appreciate your feedback. We look forward to hearing your thoughts!

notes.title: Thank You for Over 40k Wishlists (Top 700 Most Wishlisted on Steam)!
notes.notes:
Hello, I'm Shibuya from Studio Snowblind, the developer of Glaciered.

Last weekend, Glaciered acheived over [strike]30,000[/strike] 40,000 wishlists on Steam, and even got into the top [strike]1000[/strike] 700 most wishlisted games on Steam! To a small indie developer like me, it's almost hard to believe how big that number is. I would like to thank you all for your continuous support and for looking forward to the game.
(Update: We got even more wishlists, reaching 40,000 in the short time after the announcement. Thank you so much for your support!)

I try to read all the feedback you give based on your experiences with the demo. Some of it has already been reflected in the demo through updates, but some others need more time, such as adjusting the camera. I'll continue to work hard to improve on the game throughout development.

And thanks to your support, I have two exciting announcements to make today!

First, you'll be able to carry over a part of your demo save data to the full game.

If you've played the demo enough, you might have already noticed, but one of the endgames of Glaciered is to craft your very own wings and combine them with character stat growth and mutations to create various unique character builds. For players who have spent countless hours on crafting wings, we're planning on letting you carry over these wings to the full version of the game! More details will be announced in the future.

For other features such as character levels and features unlocked through memory trading, since the demo version has a different experience gain table and requires different materials, these will unfortunately not be carried over to the full game. We appreciate your understanding.

Next is about an English voice over. As a small indie creator, adding a whole new voiced language was not an easy decision to make, but thank to eveyone wishlisting the game, we can finally make it a reality!

Please look forward to the English dub as well as the Japanese one. Of course, you will be able to select the voice over and subtitle language separately to suit your preferences.

Lastly, I would like to introduce some features that will appear in the full game. First off is one of the Shard Quills you'll learn: Sniper Shard Quills.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/f4cedbd261ce4930d5b423375d17b12b2050774c.gif[/img]

Sniper Shard Quills are suited to long-range combat. They shoot a crystal shard that flies rapidly and straight ahead, which has a very long range and can pierce through multiple enemies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/9139bae2ef409b9b40a1346cfdfd0a9504aa39bb.gif[/img]

It's especially useful for ambushing enemies or when you want to whittle down the number of enemies around you quickly.

The special move Wild Barrage is an ultimate shot with even heavier damage that cannot be guarded against and can also pierce through multiple enemies. It's a very deadly attack that can completely turn the tide of battle.

Of course, the existence of powerful wings like these also means that there are formidable enemies you'll have to use them against. Most of the creatures that appear in the demo strongly resemble existing fish and prehistoric marine life, but halfway into the game, you'll start seeing an even wider variety of futuristic sea creatures.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/6f1122d529f7429121192015b43292fe65f9320e.jpg[/img]

And when it comes to the sea, how could we forget mollusks? They're still around in the seas of Glaciered, laying in wait for intruders.

Paki aren't the only crustaceans in the sea, either. You'll eventually have to fight other aggressive crustaceans who have evolved even more threateningly on your journey.

I might post about gamedev progress and teaser content in [url=https://discord.gg/g6yn9gYU69]our official Discord server[/url] from now on, so please come in and check it out if you're interested!

notes.title: Demo Update v0.7.255
notes.notes:
Hi, thank you so much for playing the demo!
Since the demo was released, we are very happy that so many people have played the demo and given us very constructive feedback.

We just released an update that includes new features, balance tweaks, and bug fixes based on community feedback.

[h1]New Features[/h1]
[h2]Resting Spot Overhaul[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/c7ff026c5d60d6405ecd38b805042b45eed30911.png[/img]
Now you can access your stash from the resting spots!
Ask our fish friend Pui, to bring the items to the hideout. So they are safe from dropping by death. The default stash space is also doubled.

You can even fast travel directly to the hideout without opening the menu. This makes patching yourself up a lot easier.

[h2]Pui deserves more love![/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/3bbec22b4f0c2e9dad8d010faa947eb723127067.png[/img]
You can now rescue your Pui by holding down the interact button close to the Pui that is playing dead.
This option is available both in and out of combat. However, you will be defenseless during the rescue, so be careful.

[h2]Tutorials only move when you move[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/78bdd8ecd300f690085795dd977a93afca320c0f.gif[/img]
You no longer have to be bothered by enemies and can read tutorials as long as you want.

[h2]Minor Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fast travel refreshes your healing count automatically.
[*] Your latest resting point is now marked on the map screen.
[*] Dodge can now cancel player's Super Stagger animation.
[*] You will notice when you have lost your rest effects and when you get healing items created by Pui.
[*] Expand the range and angle for interacting with Hideout functions, and further reduce the amount of time you need to hold down the button.
[*] Fixed the display of each stat point on the status screen to show the raw stat points and the amount increased by your wing traits separately.
[*] Now you can set the camera sensitivity for X and Y axis separately.
[*] With keyboard and mouse input, "O" now opens the Wing menu and "P" opens the Quest menu directly (keybind reset required).
[*] Slightly increased player status HUD size.
[*] Ice blocks can be destroyed by any attack, except the first ice block.
[*] Collectible points are now emit glitter particles.
[*] Shaders used in VFX are now cached at startup to avoid frame stuttering.
[/list]

[h2]Balance Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Reduced damage output of the Iski(s) that spawn in the cave of the Tranquil Trail
[*] Reduced damage area of the Reega (Male) lightning shock
[*] Reduced damage output of the [spoiler]Alpha Guedu[/spoiler]
[*] Increased the default stash space limit from 10 to 20
[*] Reduced the overall stamina consumption of various player actions.
[*] Increased the amount of stamina that Lung & Heart stat points increase.
[*] Increased the size of the hit box of the Power Attack with the Regular Blade Quill.
[/list]

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue that could cause a soft lock when players take damage while leaving resting points.
[*] Fixed an issue where the special creature variants of the [spoiler]RITE OF THE HUNT[/spoiler] quest were not randomized properly. 
[*] Fixed an issue that sometimes caused enemy AI to not reset properly.
[*] Fixed an issue where summoned weak enemies by bosses were randomly running away from combat.
[*] Fixed an issue that sometimes prevented you from moving the camera in photo mode.
[*] Fixed an issue where the Crystal Edge ability could not harvest collectibles.
[*] Fixed an issue where Pui sometimes didn't play dead even when their health was zero.
[*] Fixed an issue where the cutscene skip progress indicator would overlap with the ESC key guide.
[/list]

Thanks again, and we'd love to hear your feedback on the Steam forums and the official Discord server.

notes.title: Demo Mini-Update v0.7.249
notes.notes:
Hi, thank you so much for playing the demo.
We have added some features, bug fixes and balance adjustments based on our community feedback.

[h2]Showing Salvage Result on the Item Screen[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/5f9c8923b580be2df220060a23e6942f1c3d84b7.jpg[/img]
The items you get when salvaging a salvageable item are now displayed on the item screen. No more wasting materials because you have no idea what you will get.

[h2]Balance Changes and Small Feature Updates[/h2]
[list]
[*]The amount of healing fog released when Pui is set to assist mode has been changed from 25% of your maximum HP to a fixed 30HP. The initial design was make Pui more useful for high-level players for the production version, but 25% of maximum HP was too low for many players playing the demo version.
[*]Paging tabs on the menu screen can now be accessed with A/D or left/right directional keys when you are using keyboard + mouse control. Note that this feature may require resetting your key bindings.
[*]Stereo, Surround, 5.1ch, and 7.1ch have been added to the audio settings. Restarting application is required to apply the change.
[*]Reduced stamina consumption for dodge is reduced to 13 from 15
[/list]

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*]Additional fixes for sound crackling issues. Sound cracking during photo mode has also been addressed.
[*]Fixed an issue that sometimes caused dazzling glare when retrieving items dropped by enemies.
[/list]

Thank you so much for your feedback!

notes.title: Demo Hotfix v0.7.248
notes.notes:
Hi, thank you so much for playing the demo and giving us your valuable feedback!
This patch is very small and contains just one change; but it's impactful on the gameplay

[h3]●Taking a short rest on save points now refreshes your healing count.[/h3]

The core idea of the design was intended to remind players to return to the hideout for the long rest buffs and progressions but it was not a good idea. Instead of punishing players, there should have been an incentive to return to the base.

These incentives will not be introduced in the demo, but we decided that at least the healing restrictions that punish players should be removed. We will continue to introduce incentives in the release version.

Note that there is a line in the dialog of the unknown voice[spoiler](seeker)[/spoiler]that says something like "You must rest in the hideout to regain your healing count", but don't mind it. This requires an additional recording round and cannot be fixed for the demo version.

We really appreciate your feedback. We look forward to hearing your thoughts.

notes.title: Steam Demo Out Now! Looking Forward to Your Thoughts and Feedback!
notes.notes:
Hello! I'm Shibuya from Studio Snowblind, the developer of Glaciered.
[b]Surprise! We've released a demo for Glaciered, available right now![/b]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2486780

Over the duration of Tokyo Game Show, many players visited the PLAYISM booth to play the Glaciered event demo. Even early in the day, we already had so many visitors that we needed to give out numbered tickets for people to come back to the queue later. In order to let as many people play the game as possible, we shortened the play time of the demo as much as we could, but still we sometimes had to turn down people due to the long wait times. We're sorry we couldn't let everyone who wanted to play the game have a chance to try it out.In order to let more people try out Glaciered, we carefully discussed releasing the demo to the public, and now we're confident that the timing is right. This new demo is different from the TGS demo, removing the time limit and adding more features for further polish.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/eabebf2975bfeb2f33bd44f4c4bf11b557e2e80d.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/5b09b7d15af187f02d58c0e8d9fe4b6df11e979e.png[/img]

This demo starts from the very beginning of the full game, and features the core gameplay features of underwater battles and character growth mechanics. There is no time limit. The player character level is capped at Lv 5 in the demo, but at your base, the Seeker's Hideout, you can experience the core gameplay loop: buy and craft items, unlock a wide variety of passive skills, raise your companion the Pui, and feed a giant mussel and receive equipment upgrade items in return. And after you beat the demo, there's actually a bit more you can work towards...

This demo might be rather early for a game slotted for a 2025 release, but the main reason we're doing this is to receive feedback from our players. We're very fortunate to have a wonderful community, and we've received a lot of constructive feedback at events like BitSummit and Tokyo Game Show, which have all been very helpful. More on that later, but even so, we could only really receive feedback from within Japan, where we're based. As we've gotten wishlists from players from all over the world, we think it's important for us to get feedback from global players as well and reflect that in development.

We would love it if you could share your feedback with us on the Steam forums or the official Discord server. We'll take your opinions into consideration as we continue to work hard on development.

[url=https://discord.gg/g6yn9gYU69][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/5db1e7f1a70edeabe7b65aab4c0a43ec23930458.png[/img][/url]

[b]And yes, we have an [url=https://discord.gg/g6yn9gYU69]official Discord server[/url] now alongside the new demo![/b] Please join the server and enjoy the beginning of this futuristic adventure with us and other players!

And now that the demo is out, we would like to answer some frequently asked questions we've already received so far.

[h3]Q. Can I play this game with a controller/keyboard and mouse?[/h3]
[b]A.[/b] This game is fully playable with either a controller or a keyboard and mouse. You can use whichever control scheme you like for everything in the game, from combat to exploration. We also have various keybind settings you can change in the options. However, since the gamepad input is built on XInput, other controllers such as PS5 and Switch controllers may need some extra setup elsewhere. If you run into any problems, please tell us on the Discord server.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/0318a364b9bfc318d5f515265c7b8d7b25edb2eb.png[/img]

[h3]Q. Can I change the FOV? Can I change the graphics settings? Can I use DLSS? What's the framerate limit?[/h3]
[b]A.[/b] This game has FOV slider support as well as individual options for DLSS and V-Sync. You can select a framerate limit from the presets of 60, 120, or 240, but there is also a limitless option. As a PC gamer myself, I want to implement a wide variety of options for accessibility. If you have any more requests for options like these, please tell us on Discord.
We also support graphics card options with Standard, Low, and Lowest settings. In the full version, we're planning on implementing even higher-level ray tracing settings, but as keeping the lighting consistent during development is very time-consuming, this is not included in the demo.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/73069886a7843fe5fedb617dab4669c45e952a91.png[/img]

[h3]Q. What are the required specs for this game?[/h3]
[b]A.[/b] They're as listed on the store page. For a smooth gameplay experience, we recommend using a PC with a GPU of GTX1060 or higher, with a VRAM of 4GB or more. If you see framerate drops, please try lowering the framerate in the settings.
We have tested the game on Steam Deck, which played at an average of 30fps on the lowest graphic settings. We will continue to optimize the game until the full release.

[h3]Q. Does this game support ultrawide screens?[/h3]
[b]A.[/b] Yes, you can play this game in wide resolutions such as 32:9 and 21:9. We think it'll be thrilling to play this game with an ultrawide screen and high FOV!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/aacfd8ed096feb078227532a534c330298312bed.jpg[/img]

[h3]Q. Are the Tokyo Game Show survey results reflected in this demo?[/h3]
[b]A.[/b] We implemented a lot of your feedback in this demo. For example, we've added the ability to automatically lock onto the next enemy nearby once you've defeated the first one, made the camera automatically rotate around the player character according to their movement, swapping the A and B buttons in the UI, and more features that were requested in the survey. Of course, you can toggle all of these on or off according to your preferences in the options.

If you have any more questions, feel free to ask us on the Steam forums or the official Discord server!

notes.title: Devlog #4 Introducing the Seeker's Hideout, the Pui, and Photo Mode
notes.notes:
Hello. I'm Shibuya from Studio Snowblind, the developer of Glaciered. It's been a while since my last devlog, but the development of Glaciered is going along smoothly.

Today, I would like to introduce to you the Seeker's Hideout, which will be your main base, and the Pui, a trusty companion who will accompany you on your harsh journey across the seas.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/cf9ee32e4a3eff462b08b0e123c6d441ae256dde.png[/img]
You will encounter the Seeker early on in the game, who will later let you use the Seeker's Hideout as your base of operations. Here you will find all sorts of facilities you can use to strengthen yourself. You can rest, eat a meal, strengthen your wings (equipment), trade, and raise your companion, who I'll introduce later on in this devlog.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/8379c8d5fed3db69aa000a99a3e6b5f2a75847fe.png[/img]
This particularly large crystal is the Great Glacium Crystal, which is the equivalent to a smithy or workbench you may be familiar with in other games. Here you can spend materials to craft new wings or strengthen old ones, or use rare items to draw out the hidden abilities of your wings.

Crafting your very own unique wings and making them as powerful as possible is one of the aspects of the game you can sink many hours into if you really dig deep into the system.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/8e1b7b6ac9d8931e94e0e5ebb038538aab151f1b.png[/img]
In the center of the hideout is the Fossil Tree, which is where you can go to sleep to rest your wounds, as well as consume meals to prepare for the next part of your journey.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/a0c103a7b2ed3e47d7a6ff66049947c425599a62.png[/img]
When hunting other creatures you meet in the sea, you will sometimes obtain parts of their bodies as items. These items can be consumed before bed and will grant you powerful buffs. It's unwise to fight against strong foes without getting enough food and sleep.

Resting is one of the most important mechanics in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/9cfff1f5b1c204090cc879c629f254b0b4381f0a.png[/img]
You can also stash items in your resting place.

Whenever you're defeated in battle, you'll drop all of your held items where you were slain, but anything you have in storage will be safe. It's a good idea to stash anything important or rare in your storage before heading out.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/24efdee3029c371254a9792a2fe123da7d2469b7.png[/img]
With this giant slate, you can take part in Memory Trading. During your travels, you will be able to find Tuai memories, which you can trade in here to obtain knowledge on how to create new wings (i.e. blueprints), mutations (i.e. customizable passive skills), additional stash space, and more.

Search every crevice under the sea, or clear missions given to you by the Seeker to collect Tuai memories and trade them for your own growth.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/b82e900ea5259b946fd5aa3987afe2e590da50c8.gif[/img]
During your journey, you will be accompanied by a trusty companion called the Pui. It's a creature evolved from the pufferfish, and it has an organ on its forehead that can produce light, making it particularly reliable in the dark depths at night.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/b591d0f9b68972161431f92d64ff86bc9ff7aa6d.gif[/img]
(That's right: the sea in Glaciered goes through a day-night cycle in real time, and completely different creatures will appear depending on the time of day!)

Use the Pui to light your way as you explore the sea at night, or in dark caves where no other light reaches. However, the Pui isn't just a fancy living torch. It can follow your orders and participate in battle as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/3d15d0685b7c92befc767b6a6d52ab9f73a99968.gif[/img]
By feeding the Pui different food at the hideout, it can learn different abilities based on the creature its food comes from. For example, by eating the electric organ of a Reega, a carnivorous fish that utilizes electric attacks, it will gain the ability to discharge a burst of electricity around itself, which will let it fight alongside you against hostile creatures.

But be careful; just like you, the Pui will also be knocked out if it takes too much damage. You'll have to keep a close eye on its condition and protect it when necessary.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/d85e89a3e3491b1b1789c4e61db4214fa8d97551.gif[/img]
As a bonus, this game includes a photo mode. You can stop time whenever you want to take a picture of the underwater world 65 million years in the future. And if you manage to photograph specific creatures, the Seeker might have a reward for you...

I would love to also tell you about other game features such as the fast travel system, the wide range of passive skills, and new formidable bosses, but this will be all for today's devlog.

By the way, I'm currently discussing with the publisher PLAYISM about the possibility of releasing a demo for the game.

Obviously I would love to get valuable feedback from you all as soon as possible in order to polish the game even further, but at the same time, I want to share a demo that's as well-made as it can be, so we're still trying to figure out the best timing to release the demo.

When we're ready to release a demo, we'll announce here on Steam as well as on social media, so please wishlist the game and follow us to get the latest updates!

notes.title: Devlog #3 Action Gameplay Mostly Complete! New Creature Designs and Gameplay Rev
notes.notes:
Hello, I’m Shibuya from Studio Snowblind, the developer of Glaciered. Today, I’ll share some information on our development progress.

The core action gameplay is mostly complete, and right now I’m working on the various creatures and stages to flesh out the world of the game. In this devlog, I’ll share some of that with you all.

[h2]About the Creatures[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/952219cd409bfb4a9c25b44ccc2b48d9818ba02c.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/5a4e8f483b9b37b8fd591da9009fb6fd3840ac6a.png[/img]

The [b]Diye[/b] is a type of shark that has developed a thick armor around its skull. It can’t swim very fast and moves sluggishly, but it relentlessly chases down its enemies and weakens them until it can swallow them whole. Its tough head armor deflects all kinds of attacks, and also acts as a powerful weapon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/bcf55a073dd1560d26882bcd137a17e01fc7408e.gif[/img]

Beware of its rock-hard headbutts and bites if you want to get out in one piece. The key to victory is to find the more vulnerable parts of its body to attack.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/38a715257d47e4f656f332aa16b2d22b99ebacd4.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/c8f943c15715d4d171acd4408994d22c4577b2d9.png[/img]
The [b]Paki[/b] is a type of arthropod that evolved from Japanese horseshoe crabs and resembles sea scorpions. They usually prey on smaller arthropods attached to plankton and seaweed, but their highly territorial and aggressive nature makes them very dangerous.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/784dccdcb2d8453a830cd72a17ad2d6a0e4e11b9.gif[/img]

It’s a swift swimmer with sensitive sensory organs that it uses to sense the vibrations in the water and detect the movements of incoming enemies. It nimbly dodges the player’s attacks and uses the poisonous spikes on its tail to fight back. If you try to chase one down without thinking, it might turn the tables on you. If you’re going to fight one, you’ll have to be extra careful in deciding when to strike.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/87218d36a14b3c745ea241b76a2694814f9c7511.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/388c8009a672315b9ab4410519b62064378a64c8.png[/img]
The [b]Iski[/b] is a creature that evolved from a relative of the sea ruffe. It’s characterized by the highly-developed spines on its tail. When stressed, the Iski’s tail muscles react and send the spines flying out of its tail at the speed of bullets.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/07206d460868f27cb7ed0ccae4089b9e42cfc505.gif[/img]

Anyone who tries to prey on an Iski from behind will surely get a painful face-full of spines. The Iski is a pretty fragile creature, but it will try to quickly swim away from the player, making it harder to land attacks on it.

Apart from the above, there are many more creatures from the future that will appear in this game. And even though I’ve only shown hostile creatures so far, there are other non-hostile creatures that live in the same sea. They might be able to help you on your journey if you know how to use them well.

All of the creatures I've introduced today appear in an area called the Sea of Tranquility. It’s an area with a rich and varied ecosystem which serves as the first place the player will explore when they start the game. We’ve been going through a lot of trial and error for the level design of this area, so we can’t show you anything just yet, but we’re working hard to make it a sea worthy of exploration.

[h2]New Features Revealed in Special Indie Game Livestreams[/h2]

[previewyoutube=gjCAP0iM1Is;full][/previewyoutube]
I’ve gotten the help of some streamers to further showcase these new features.

In this [url=https://www.youtube.com/live/gjCAP0iM1Is?feature=shared]fei CHANNEL livestream[/url], you can see battles with the new enemies such as the Diye and Paki, as well as some new abilities that I couldn’t go over in this article. What’s more, this stream features an interview between me and fei, where I talk a bit about the world of Glaciered, so please check it out.
(Note: The livestream is in Japanese)

Furthermore, Glaciered was featured on Iseijin Channel’s [url=https://www.youtube.com/live/pPGdrvhdJ5w?feature=shared&t=12250]""1st INDIE GAME INTRODUCTION LIVE""[/url], a two-day event featuring several indie game creators. I talked about my inspirations and the parts I’m working hard on, so please give it a listen if you’re interested!
(Note: The livestream is in Japanese)

[h2]TOW Joins the Music Team![/h2]

Lastly, I’m excited to announce that the Japanese acoustic band TOW will be working with us on the soundtrack of Glaciered!

[previewyoutube=9Xn-u0KYkwM;full][/previewyoutube]
TOW is an acoustic band with a distinctive Oriental style and powerful vocals that has been gaining attention from around the world. As the producer of Sumire, I’ve known them ever since they wrote the music for that game back in the day, and I’ve had the chance to listen to them perform in live concerts. There, I was blown away by the range of expressions in their music; besides the gentle, melancholic feeling of the music in Sumire, they also expressed the strength and harshness of life through their music, and that is why I approached them again to ask if they could compose for Glaciered.

I believe that TOW is one of the only bands that can capture this world set in the distant future, where various creatures desperately fight for survival in a place unlike Asia, or Europe, or any other place in our world. Please look forward to their music as well!

notes.title: Devlog #2「BitSummit Let’s Go!!」Report and an Intro to the Gear System
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/25649cc1be82bd91885db5bb3af90d334b9aa671.png[/img]
BitSummit Let's Go!!, one of the biggest indie game events in Japan, was held in Kyoto from July 14 to July 16. Glaciered participated in the event too with a playable demo, so in this devlog we'll share what happened at the event!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/dfd336a69131fb0f09b2c5f755021ee584b1ea20.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/1ad1e8390e1d8148ad416ada06db0a25fcdc7418.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/7f4a51551d0d486c287baf336c0cd00af0895a7d.png[/img]
We provided two ways to play the demo – on the PC, and on the Steam Deck. Our booth was pretty small, but we put up an eye-catching banner and played gameplay videos on our monitors, and thankfully it was enough to attract visitors to stop and look at the game! We were also really happy to hear some visitors say that they came to play Glaciered, or that they were interested in the game before the event.

The demo was a part of the tutorial, from the beginning of the Sea of Tranquility stage to a mid-stage boss fight. We wanted to let players get a feeling for the gameplay and the core action elements, as well as explore the seas of the future.

On days that were open to the general public, there were a lot of visitors who wanted to try the game, so there were times we had to restrict players to only playing for around 15 minutes. Partly because of this, only around 30% of players could clear the demo. We're sorry that many players couldn't play as much of the game as they wanted, but we hope that the demo helped players understand and experience the appeal of Glaciered for themselves!

We also got visited by reporters from several Japanese game media sites, such as 4Gamer, Game*Spark, Den Faminico Gamer, and Indie Freaks. They tried out the game and even did some developer interviews, so please check out their articles at the following links! (Articles are in Japanese)

[b]・[Play Report] We tried out the Underwater Soulslike Action Glaciered. Sharks are Super Strong 65 Million Years in the Future! (4Gamer)[/b]
https://www.4gamer.net/games/646/G064644/20230715018/


[b]・You Can't Let Your Guard Down in the Futuristic Fight for Survival in Glaciered...! Demo Play Report & Developer Interview on One Guy's Deep Love for Science Fiction (Game*Spark)[/b]
https://www.gamespark.jp/article/2023/07/16/132098.html


[b]・"Soar" Freely in the Frozen Seas in Glaciered, a Love Letter to Science Fiction. Explore a Future Earth, Home to Highly-Evolved Creatures (DenfaminicoGamer)[/b]
https://news.denfaminicogamer.jp/kikakuthetower/230714t


[b]・Press Report on Glaciered,  the Game where you Face Futuristic Underwater Threats (Indie Freaks)[/b]
https://www.indie-freaks.com/2023/07/bitsummit2023-glaciered/

[previewyoutube=Ik8Szdmmobc;full][/previewyoutube]

What's more, our developer Kei Shibuya was featured on Day 2 (7/16) of "Always Live Together@Bitsummit 2023", the IGN Japan livestream that went on during the entirety of the event. You can see him [url=https://www.youtube.com/live/Ik8Szdmmobc?feature=share&t=1850]here, starting from 30:50[/url]!

[h1] On a scale from 1 to 5, what would you rate the overall experience of the demo?[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/f80b718afe32ef1e838de875efc3018c114abf7c.png[/img]

We also did a little online survey that anyone who tried out the game could fill in if they wanted to. We're glad to share that we got quite a lot of positive responses, and we were reassured that the developer's vision for the game lined up with players' expectations for it! We also received a lot of feedback about the gameplay, including the gamefeel of the tutorial, difficulty settings, and the visibility of resting spots (save points), which provided a lot of valuable insight that we'll put to good use in future development. A huge thank you to everyone who took the time to fill out the survey!

We don't know the next time Glaciered will be playable in a public event like this just yet,  but we'll make sure to prepare an even better demo for next time, so please stay tuned!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/64bde42b75593593ded9ce76a0cfbfedd835bbb9.png[/img]

While we're here, we'll also introduce a feature of the game that players could experience in the event demo.

In the past few months, the dev team has been focusing on the character progression system. It's a system that will make Glaciered's characteristic underwater action even more in-depth. Some people might call it an RPG-esque feature. Let's see what it looks like!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/5d169bf16385a2d59e115a8612256e3f187e3b28.png[/img]

Glaciered has something of a gear system, which is the customization of your "Crystal Wings". The player character has wings that consist of the primary "Blade Quills" which are hard and tough to break, and the secondary "Shard Quills" which can detatch from the body easily. Blade Quills are used for melee attacks, while Shard Quills are used for ranged attacks. Over the course of your journey and through battles against powerful foes, you'll learn new types of Quills that you can use to strengthen yourself.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/d67c4ae28d7422e7c160cd8f4deb6876a606a767.gif[/img]

Changing your wings also changes the way you move around in combat. For example, Piercing Blade Quills specialize in thrusting and piercing attacks. They can deal high damage and give you a great boost forward, but you might have trouble landing hits on more agile enemies that will avoid your attacks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/ba4e8fb2268629e7b5df485000d7d53a2070ea45.gif[/img]

Changing your Shard Quills will change your ranged attacks. For example, Splitting Shard Quills can split into a barrage of small crystal shards that shoot towards your target. (Kind of like a shotgun!) They have a shorter range than other quills, but they hit extremely hard once you're close enough to your target. If you enjoy getting right up in your opponent's face in a fight, these quills are for you.

Furthermore, if you hold the ranged attack button, your ranged attack will turn into a special attack.

For example, Splitting Shard Quills allow you to use the special attack Suspended Crystals, which first surrounds you with small crystals, then shoots all of them into the next enemy you land an attack on. You could pair this with your ranged attack to keep an enemy away, or combo it with melee attacks for even more attacking options.

You can change the Blade Quills and Shard Quills on both the left and right wings. You can attack instantly with either wing, so you can mix and match all sorts of Quills to find the perfect combination that fits your playstyle.

Quills also differ by rarity, and some of the rarest quills have unique abilities... Defeating strong foes that lurk in the seas and collecting rare quills is one of the ways players can really sink their teeth into this game.

There's more character progression in this game than just the quills, but we'll introduce them another time. Until then, please wishlist us and keep an eye out for updates! See you soon!

notes.title: Announcing Publisher, and more!
notes.notes:
I'm Shibuya from Studio Snowblind, the developer of this game. I have great news to share with you all today: PLAYISM is going to be the publisher of Glaciered!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/21da14c37c380cca97e101c661ccc35b329805bf.jpg[/img]

Ever since we announced Glaciered last July, we've received so many offers from different publishers, almost 20 of them! This was way more than I could even imagine. I'm extremely thankful that this game, which started as a small solo project, gathered so much attention from publishers all around the world. I'll take this opportunity to say a big thank you to everyone who contacted me about this game.

Although I was approached by many publishers, in the end I can only sign a contract with one of them. This was a very difficult choice for me, but I know that PLAYISM does great work, and when they reached out to me, I almost immediately decided to accept their offer.

PLAYISM has published a lot of incredible indie titles such as Bright Memory, Fight Crab, and DEEEER Simulator: Your Average Everyday Deer Game. They also handle localization, and I hardly have the space to list out all the game localizations they've done!

In the past, I've worked as an indie game publisher and localizer as well. PLAYISM's localizations are consistently top-notch quality, and as someone in the same industry, I aimed to be more like them in my own work as well. One of my favorite games, Night in the Woods, is also one of the many games localized by PLAYISM. I was so astounded by the high quality of the Japanese localization that I couldn't stop myself from sending PLAYISM an email thanking them for their work.

Glaciered is a single-player game, and I want high-quality translations for its characters and world in as many languages as possible, ones that can preserve the nuances of the original Japanese, my mother tongue. This is one of my main wishes for this game, especially since localization is one of the most important parts of the gamedev process. And I'm absolutely positive that PLAYISM's localization will grant my wish.

What's more, I've decide to increase the number of available languages. At first, I only planned on implementing Japanese and English, but now we will be adding Traditional and Simplified Chinese, French, Italian, German, and Spanish localizations to the game.

Nowadays, I'm not the only one working on Glaciered anymore. This is all thanks to the people and resources I've managed to gather for this project. But of course, this is still an indie game, and it's far from having the same production value as a AAA title, but I'm very excited at how far we've come.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/f712590677fba3cf5833ce17058bdc76073c11d0.png[/img]Artworks by [url=https://www.facebook.com/HPLGameDesign]HPL Game Design[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/be3dbf283ce675fa67baa57ad2648ad685e4232d.png[/img]Artworks by [url=https://cgart.com/]CG - Art Creation[/url]

Besides this, we might even be able to release the game on platforms other than Steam, which is to say consoles. There's nothing I can announce just yet, but I'll do so once we've gotten some concrete plans ready to share with you all, so please hang in there while we figure things out.

I have another exciting announcement to make: Glaciered was introduced in the INDIE Live Primiere corner of the INDIE Live Expo! And we've made a brand new trailer for the occasion. Take a look!

[previewyoutube=t9EL_zK8Ylo;full][/previewyoutube]

[previewyoutube=TynONRumHew;full][/previewyoutube]

This trailer showcases an important feature—the Murk, the "night" of the ocean. It also shows off some new actions that you can unlock through character progression. I'm planning on elaborating on character progression in particular in a future devlog.

notes.title: Glaciered Devlog #1 : Underwater Combat
notes.notes:
Hello, I am Shibuya from Studio Snowblind, the (solo) developer of Glaciered. Today I have released a new teaser featuring one of the main gameplay of the game, combat takes place in the 65 million years distant underwater.

[previewyoutube=gJimL7_Ibpk;full][/previewyoutube]

Let me introduce myself a little bit, I was a former producer of Project Nimbus : Complete Edition, a fast-paced mech action indie game, also involved to a lot of action games including consoles in past. One of the goal I am trying to achieve with this game is "three-dimensional combat with a sense of speed and strategy".

Our sense of speed is relative. Distance between the player character and the camera, and the objects in between, as well as the camera FOV, determine the sense of speed. One of the reasons why I pick underwater for this game is that I can place a large number of objects with proper context, which are indicators of speed. By trying to emphasize a sense of speed by only using backgrounds, the speed of the player character becomes too fast, and the strategic aspect will be lost.

In Glaciered, visual effects such as marine snow, fish, and bubbles give players a sense of speed, keeping the speed reasonable. It would be great if the combat could have a good balance between dynamics and strategy.

This new teaser features two carnivorous species of fish. They already showed up in the first announcement trailer, but let me introduce them!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/b06e1e10ae3ae976f7e939028399037044e7b83d.jpg[/img]

Reega, a carnivorous fish that is widely distributed in the ocean. They have long fangs, which they use to bite randomly, inflicting serious trauma to preys. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/477aff41c3cd25aed9c8d576ee85d961050e3c0d.gif[/img]

They also exhibit a pronounced sexual dimorphism. and males do not develop fangs, but instead possess organic electric organs. Watch out the powerful electric attacks produced by that!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42707393/b7bdf91f254a161b3c0ceff46ad3e433363f8d79.jpg[/img]

Guedu, an apex predator that has dominated the Earth's oceans since our timeline and even before. Each attack from this mass of muscle can be lethal. Be cautious and precise, find a chance, then strike through it with your wings.

Glaciered is in development very actively. Check out the official Twitter account for more information. I'm exciting to introduce more things about the game in future!

notes.title: Glaciered is an aquatic action game set 65 million years in the future where you play an ass-kicking ninja fish-bird
notes.notes: t first, I thought Glaciered resembled a big-budget spiritual successor to Abzû. The trailer for the newly announced game, which sees you exploring an entirely oceanic Earth 65 million years in the future, starts with its bizarre fish-bird protagonist (known as Tuai, apparently) gliding effortlessly through stunning underwater locations. Beneath the giant glacier that covered this far-future Earth, your Tuai flits through underwater caves and carves pathways through carpets of seagrass. It looking beautiful, charming, and relaxing, a glorious chillout adventure in the vein of Giant Squid's mini-masterpiece... Read more.
